name: Tabstack

modes.label: Native product meter; not a general-purpose 4-vCPU/8-GiB VM
modes.note: Not auto-rankable for generic VM workloads. Native price and usage limits are preserved in provider rate_cards/extras and regimes. Empty sizes intentionally prevents inventing CPU/RAM capacity or treating missing rates as zero.

plans.name: Starter
plans.note: 100,000 credits/month; $0.30/1,000 overage; Fast research. Default $100 monthly cap/400k credits. Default cap = 300,000 overage credits beyond the 100k included ($100/month ceiling including the fee), then requests stop. Rate limit 15 requests/min per account (Trial 10, Team 25, Pro 100); no daily/hourly cap; higher limits via support.

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.note: Custom API quotas, support and SLA.

plans.name: Trial
plans.note: 10,000 one-time free credits, no card; 10 requests/minute; no overage - requests stop when credits run out, never bills.

features.ip_note: Country geotargeting routes requests through a proxy in the chosen country, but proxy type (datacenter/residential), pricing and default egress are undocumented; agents identify as "Mozilla-Tabstack/1.0" and respect robots.txt.

caveats: No vCPU/RAM SKU or hourly browser rental offered on reviewed pricing; unsuitable as raw VM substitute.
Automate and Research charge per action; one task may execute many actions.
Plan requests/minute are Trial10/Starter15/Team25/Pro100; simultaneous active-task concurrency not established.
10,000 trial credits cannot be represented as $10 of compute credit; do not monetize without specifying endpoint mix.
Native billing cannot be reduced to a 4-vCPU/8-GiB price. No matching engine sizes, by design.

fleet.notes: Action-based browser/data API rather than VM fleet. Trial/Starter/Team/Pro request-per-minute limits 10/15/25/100 are not concurrent running tasks or instances. Enterprise custom API quotas; no active fleet count documented.

snapshot_auto.note: Stateless per-call API ('Tabstack is a stateless per-call API'). No machine or browser session survives a call.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: Tabstack is a stateless per-call API. It scales horizontally with your request volume, but there are no managed browser sessions to configure
snapshot_on_demand.note: Nothing to snapshot; no session/profile/context persistence API.

own_agent_api.quote: `client.agent.automate(...)` returns a stream of typed events that you iterate with `for await ... of` (TypeScript) or `for ... in` (Python), with no SSE framing to parse yourself.
own_agent_api.note: Drives Tabstack's OWN hosted browser agent (not Claude Code/Codex/OpenCode): POST /v1/automate with a natural-language task + url + guardrails, streams SSE events (task:*, agent:action, browser:navigated, complete). Mid-task follow-up is limited to interactive-mode form data via POST /v1/automate/{requestId}/input. There is no list/resume of past agent conversations; each call is a one-shot run (10-min SDK timeout). /research is a similar one-shot research agent.

guest_firewall.quote: Tabstack takes a URL and returns structured data - the extraction, reasoning, and research happen inside the API call before the response comes back.
guest_firewall.note: API-only product: users get no shell, root or browser/CDP access, so they cannot configure a firewall.

secret_proxy.quote: The agent fills form fields directly without exposing user-provided values to the LLM, keeping sensitive data like passwords and personal information private.
secret_proxy.note: No credential-injecting egress proxy. Credentials can be passed as the automate `data` object or supplied mid-task in interactive mode. They are typed into page form fields in Tabstack's browser, hidden from the LLM but not from the browser. Data-handling page: 'Interactive form values are always ephemeral. They expire within minutes and are never stored.' HTTP only (browser forms); nothing for other protocols.
